title: Power Rankings: Hawks take top spot
heading: 2014-15 Power Rankings: Week 10
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: This is the latest in a season that the Hawks -- on pace to win a franchise-record 62 games -- have topped the East since this committee (of one) started covering the NBA in 1993-94. The same season, as noted last week, when the Hawks stunningly dealt Dominique Wilkins for Danny Manning on deadline day.

rankings.summaryHtml: Splash Brothers Update: Steph Curry ranks second among PGs in PER at 26.9, trailing only Russell Westbrook's gaudy 31.7 (in 12 fewer games thanks to Russ' hand injury). Among SGs, meanwhile, Klay Thompson is fourth at 19.8,  behind James Harden (27.2), Dwyane Wade (24.5) and Jimmy Butler (22.5).

rankings.summaryHtml: While Carmelo Anthony is ailing in NYC after snubbing the Bulls in free agency, Pau Gasol is having a turn-back-the-clock season teeming with blocked shots. Jimmy Butler, meanwhile, is up to 21.9 PPG, 6.2 RPG and 40.0 MPG ... plateaus only LeBron James has reached in the past 10 seasons.

rankings.summaryHtml: Saturday night's home L to Atlanta snuffed out any Portland hopes of ascending to No. 1. The consolation: Damian Lillard begins the week ranked sixth in the whole league in win shares at 5.8, behind only James Harden (7.0), Anthony Davis (6.7), Chris Paul (6.3), Jimmy Butler (6.1) and Steph Curry (6.0).

rankings.summaryHtml: The Mavs were a mere 20th in defensive efficiency when Rajon Rondo arrived, allowing 105.1 points per 100 possessions. In the seven games since, Dallas has been in the upper third. P.S. Dirk Nowitzki is just 13 points shy of passing Moses Malone for seventh on the NBA's career scoring chart.

rankings.summaryHtml: You look at the standings and see the Grizz at a robust 24-9 despite playing without Z-Bo (knee) for the past seven games and you have to applaud. Yet you also can't ignore that the Spurs, stuck down at No. 7 in the West, have almost the same nightly point differential as Memphis (plus-3.8 compared with plus-3.7).

rankings.summaryHtml: You've all heard the stat by now, but it still bears repeating because of the rarity of it all: San Antonio's 8-10 record in December marked just the third losing month in Tim Duncan's career. Pop said early on that it was the worst month he'd ever seen, schedule-wise; five OT games didn't hurt his case.

rankings.summaryHtml: Atlanta totes seven straight W's over West teams, including four in a row on the road, into Staples Center on Monday. The Clips, sitting at a modest 8-9 against .500-or-better teams, could use a statement W.  Spencer Hawes is finally back from injury to add a contrast to rebound machine DeAndre Jordan.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Rockets, for the record, insist they did not promise a starting spot to Josh Smith as various rival contenders vying for Smith believed. But Kevin McHale has since moved him to the bench after four starts. Houston surely had to gamble on J-Smoove at a bargain price, but the addition has been less than seamless.

rankings.summaryHtml: No one has ever referred to DeMar DeRozan as a defensive specialist. But there's no disputing the notion that the Raps regressed defensively in December without him and need the jolt of energy DeRozan's projected return this week will provide, even if Toronto went a passable 11-7 without him.

rankings.summaryHtml: Scariest No. 8 Seed Of All Time Update: OKC is 9-2 and outscoring the opposition by 15.7 points per 100 possessions when both Kevin Durant and Russell Westbrook are in uniform. Overall, though, OKC is just 1-7 against last season's West playoff teams and 3-9 in games decided by six or fewer points.

rankings.summaryHtml: As good as the Archie Goodwin detonation over Jonas Valanciunas made folks feel in the desert, Phoenix has to wonder how much damage has been done by its 1-6 record in games decided by three or fewer points. The No. 8 Suns' lead over No. 10 OKC, as of Monday morning, was down to two games.

rankings.summaryHtml: Did you know that Anthony Davis (PER: 31.4) is now 4-for-4 in his NBA career on go-ahead shot attempts in the final 24 seconds of the fourth quarter or overtime? Or perhaps we should pose the question in the manner preferred by Bill Simmons and frustrated Pels fans: Does Monty Williams know that stat?

rankings.summaryHtml: John Wall (17.2 PPG, 10.3 APG) is on pace to join Rod Strickland (1997-98) as the only PGs in team history to average 15-plus PPG and 10-plus APG in a single season. What he surely wants right now, though, is a win over Chicago on ESPN this Friday night thanks to his career mark of 0-5 in head-to-heads with Derrick Rose.

rankings.summaryHtml: Four straight road wins to give the East a whopping six teams with winning records away from home. Continued growth from Giannis Antetokounmpo and, of late, John Henson. The young Bucks are just playing right through the Jabari Parker (injury) and Larry Sanders (personal matters) distractions.

rankings.summaryHtml: If LeBron is ready and rested for the season's second half after this two-week tuneup, David Blatt can presumably live with whatever happens while he's out now that he has management's public backing. Still waiting to play his first game as a 30-year-old, LeBron has never missed more than five in a row.

rankings.summaryHtml: After two successive springs delivered Heat versus Pacers in the Eastern Conference finals, Miami suddenly finds itself dueling with Indy for the East's No. 8 seed. Maybe going on the road for six games will spark the Heat, who've been better away (8-8) than they've looked on the Biscayne Bay (7-12).

rankings.summaryHtml: The Nets would be over .500 and in possession of a legit healthy cushion for a playoff spot ahead of what passes for the chasing pack if not for an 0-3 mark against Miami. rankings.summaryHtml: We're starting to get those increased doses of Rudy Gobert next to Derrick Favors in support of Gordon Hayward. Six in the past eight games, to be exact, with only a couple of cupcakes in that stretch.

rankings.summaryHtml: The timing of the Mike Malone firing, which had so many people puzzled when it happened, only looks worse now with the Kings cratering under Ty Corbin. For all the undeniable philosophical differences between coach and management, Malone was reaching Boogie Cousins. Can Corbin?

rankings.summaryHtml: The Hornets technically remain within sight of playoff contention no matter how far under. 500 they sit. The reality, though, is that Charlotte -- unlike Detroit after Stan Van Gundy's liberated crew just reeled off five straight double-digit wins -- is far from upbeat after losing Al Jefferson (groin) for a month.

rankings.summaryHtml: A home defeat to Detroit to close out the calendar year, followed by two more losses at home to Brooklyn and Charlotte to launch 2015, is the last thing Orlando's bid to hang around the top eight needed. Next up is a four-game trip ... followed (ugh) by a Houston/Memphis/Oklahoma City homestand.

rankings.summaryHtml: The saddest part about Rajon Rondo's triumphant return wasn't solely that Celts fans hadn't seen that Rondo for the last several months of his Boston stay. Almost as bad: Rondo's return happened so soon after the trade and might have been the last game of consequence at TD Garden this season.

rankings.summaryHtml: The lowest total of home wins for any team in a single season is the five mustered by the infamous 9-73 Sixers of 1972-73. These Sixers -- mired at 0-14 in Philly but with a Jan. 21 date to host the Knicks drawing closer -- will have to go 6-21 at home for the rest of the season to avoid establishing a new low.

rankings.summaryHtml: After a 1-15 December and a 1-21 skid overall, only one thing can salvage 2014-15 for the Knicks: landing the No. 1 pick in the 30th anniversary draft since lucking into Patrick Ewing. In the meantime, with the Knicks not even cracking 90 points these days, who could dare argue with sitting Melo?
